realTimingYardstick.method: Ran depth-warm-city-batch.mjs --row-id=Bastrop --dry-run at limit=50 and limit=500, and --city-cohort --limit=500, against the live stores.
findings: Bulk-load phase dominates and is roughly FIXED regardless of batch size: 161,152ms (50-parcel run), 97,894ms (500-parcel county-wide run), 120,300ms (500-parcel city-cohort run, cityParcelUniverse=17217) -- all single-digit minutes, driven by road/BCAD/txgio geometry prefetch (roadsLoaded: 30,882 each run).
Per-parcel compute after bulk-load is cheap: msPerParcel 11-35 depending on run.
Extrapolation basis for a full county rollout: ~2-3 minutes fixed setup, then well under a second per additional parcel -- a real, usable number for sizing a 6-county rollout.

realCoverageNumbers_majorFinding.originalPremise: Pilot brief: 'currently only Bastrop has any coverage, and even that's partial -- ~4,158 of ~62,256 real accounts.'
realCoverageNumbers_majorFinding.whatWasFound: 62,260 active buildable-envelope atoms exist for Bastrop county today -- near-total raw coverage, not ~4,158. But cross-referencing against parcel-node status revealed why the original framing undercounted differently than expected: of the 62,256, only 4,552 (384 buildable + 336 provisional-front-edge + 3,832 no-buildable-area) are keyed to a CURRENTLY ACTIVE parcel-node. 57,704 (92.7%) are keyed to a parcel-node that has since been RETIRED -- computed against geometry/identity superseded by a later txgio_parcel re-acquisition.
realCoverageNumbers_majorFinding.realCurrentValidCoverage: 720 parcels (384 buildable + 336 provisional-front-edge) out of 4,694 active parcel-nodes (15.3%) have a real, currently-valid usable envelope. 3,832 (81.6%) of the active population honestly decline no-buildable-area -- plausible small-lot/oversized-setback outcomes, not spot-verified against ground truth in this pass.
realCoverageNumbers_majorFinding.interpretation: The original '~4,158 of ~62,256' figure appears to be the total buildable-outcome atom count (3,935, close but not exact, possibly measured at a different time or including provisional) without accounting for how many are keyed to now-retired geometry. Real, currently-trustworthy 'buildable' coverage is closer to 720 -- roughly an order of magnitude smaller than the headline raw-atom-count number, and this matters directly for scoping any statewide backfill: raw atom existence is not the same as current validity.

the20SampleGap.finding: Not a bug. declines['already-promoted']: 20 is a separate counter from failureBuckets (updated at a different code site, line ~796 vs the bucket-classification sites), which is why summing failureBuckets alone left an apparent 20-sample gap. cortexApiLdtConsumerVerification_confirm.question: doc-repo-bd's own stated 'real open question': does legacy-design-tools' buildableEnvelope/derive.ts + fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts correctly read the new atoms?
cortexApiLdtConsumerVerification_confirm.answer: NO -- confirmed, not assumed. Read derive.ts and its real production caller (routes/brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts:887): deriveBuildableEnvelope({ring, table, district, labeling}) independently RE-COMPUTES the envelope from raw parcel geometry plus LDT's own setback-table resolution (lib/buildableEnvelope/authoritativeSetbackSource.ts -- grepped directly, zero references to the atom chain anywhere in that file). fetchPropertyAtomChain() IS called in the route (line 1063) but its result is used ONLY as a last-resort DISTRICT fallback (line 1075-1080, only when both live GIS zoning and 'spine zoning' resolution are absent) -- never for setback feet values, never for geometry. For parcel 48021:105032, LDT would compute its own independent area/shape rather than reading the engine's 9,160 sqft result; agreement between the two is untested and not architecturally guaranteed.
cortexApiLdtConsumerVerification_confirm.significance: A real, structural maintenance-liability gap -- two independent implementations of the same derivation, exactly what the atom-first architecture exists to avoid. Matches and confirms concretely what the Aug 31 supervisor review had already self-flagged as out of its own scope ('LDT boundaryEdgeFactRead still copies edge provenance... Gold 34137 C7 still needs LDT').

noRefreshPathByDesign.question: doc-repo-bd's separate architectural question: does any path, even manual, exist to refresh a buildable-envelope atom once its parcel-node retires?
noRefreshPathByDesign.answer: NO. packages/engine-core/src/parcel-node/reconcile-county-parcel-nodes.ts's own header is explicit and deliberate: retirement is 'retire without successor... until a succession matcher is decided' -- a one-way design choice, not an oversight (a supersedes edge requires evidence of A-becomes-B that the current pipeline does not attempt to derive). It also does not cascade: directly confirmed via query that buildable-envelope atoms stay status:'active' even after their parcel-node retires (that is the 57,704-atom population above). So today there is no automatic refresh, no designed manual refresh mechanism, and the downstream atom does not even know its own input has gone stale.
noRefreshPathByDesign.implication: Every county backfilled under the current architecture will decay toward this same 90%+-stale-atom pattern over time as parcels are naturally re-platted/re-numbered by the county source. This is a bigger, permanent, recurring problem, not a one-time backfill gap -- a real architectural question for the operator to weigh, not something addressed in this pass.

travisMinimalRowScoping.minimalRowNeeds: Before a Travis row can be authored safely: (1) design + implement the geo_id_or_address_crosswalk JoinKey strategy in the cohort loader (real code, not config), (2) resolve or explicitly accept the TCAD-vs-StratMap count divergence, (3) then author the row against the live TCAD MapServer source confirmed reachable above. This is its own real scoping-sized card, same shape as Lockhart's spatial-join gap, not something to build inline here.

toolsAndAccess: gcloud (session auth, project hauska-prod-497015) for CORTEX_DATABASE_URL / ATOMS_DATABASE_URL / HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY secrets; psql for direct read-only DB queries (SET default_transaction_read_only = on for every session); npx tsx to run depth-warm-city-batch.mjs in --dry-run mode against live stores (no writes); curl for live ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer checks and the deployed hauska-retrieval-api call.
recommendationForOperator: The pilot justified itself: real coverage is much thinner than the raw atom count suggested (720 currently-valid vs 62,256 raw), a second real consumer defect exists (cortex-api/LDT never reads the engine's envelope atom), and the retirement mechanism has no refresh path by design -- meaning any future backfill decays the same way over time without a separate fix. Recommend the operator weigh a succession/refresh mechanism as a prerequisite (or at least a named, accepted risk) before committing to a statewide backfill program, alongside the already-identified per-county onboarding gaps (Lockhart's spatial join, Travis's join-key + count-divergence, Hays/McLennan/Williamson's from-scratch city onboarding).
